ps22-16-textual-question.label: Contested
ps22-16-textual-question.title: Psalm 22:16: 'like a lion' or 'pierced'?

readings.witness: Masoretic Text (standard Hebrew text), Ps 22:17 in Hebrew numbering
Septuagint (Greek translation, pre-Christian), Ps 21:17 LXX (= Ps 22:16)
A few Hebrew manuscripts, including the Nahal Hever psalms scroll (5/6HevPs)
readings.meaning: a verb form, often understood as 'they dug' or 'they pierced'

ps22-16-textual-question.explanation: The standard Hebrew text reads ka'ari, which usually means 'like a lion', giving the line 'like a lion, my hands and my feet.' The ancient Greek translation reads 'they dug', and a few Hebrew manuscripts, including a psalms scroll found at Nahal Hever near the Dead Sea, have a verb form, ka'aru, instead. The two Hebrew spellings differ by one small letter. Translations differ: the BSB, like many English Bibles, reads 'they have pierced my hands and feet', while Jewish translations generally follow 'like a lion.' Scholars still debate which reading is original. Either way, the psalm describes a sufferer surrounded and attacked.
ps22-16-textual-question.status_note: Our team has not confirmed which Nahal Hever plate shows this verse; the plate identification is unconfirmed.

references.title: Peter W. Flint, 5/6HevPs edition, Journal of Jewish Studies 51 (2000)
